title: Add MIT License to the project
feat: add GitHub Action wrapper for with-workbench
description:
## Summary

Adds `action.yml` so `with-workbench` can be used as a composite GitHub Action:

```yaml
- uses: posit-dev/with-workbench@main
  with:
    license-key: ${{ secrets.WORKBENCH_LICENSE }}
    version: "2026.01.1"
```

This mirrors the pattern established by `posit-dev/with-connect`, which already has an `action.yml`.

### Why

The CLI tool requires `uv tool install git+https://github.com/posit-dev/with-workbench.git`, which fails in GitHub Actions because the repo is internal — the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't clone it. As a composite action (`uses:`), GitHub handles the checkout natively with org-level access.

### Inputs/Outputs

**Inputs:** `license-key`, `version`, `image`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `quiet`, `stop`

**Outputs:** `WORKBENCH_URL`, `WORKBENCH_USER`, `WORKBENCH_PASSWORD`, `CONTAINER_ID`

### Usage

```yaml
- name: Start Workbench
  id: workbench
  uses: posit-dev/with-workbench@main
  with:
    license-key: ${{ secrets.WORKBENCH_LICENSE }}
    version: "2026.01.1"
    user: testuser
    password: "TestPass123!"

- name: Stop Workbench
  if: always()
  uses: posit-dev/with-workbench@main
  with:
    stop: ${{ steps.workbench.outputs.CONTAINER_ID }}
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify action works in a consuming workflow (posit-dev/vip has a companion PR)

title: fix: fail loudly when an image pull breaks mid-stream
description:
### What

`pull_image()` reported success for pulls that had actually failed.

The Docker daemon reports a mid-pull failure as an `error` chunk in the *body* of the `/images/create` stream, not as an HTTP error status. `client.api.pull()` calls `_raise_for_status` on the initial response only, before streaming begins, so it has already returned successfully by the time the pull breaks. Our loop inspected chunks solely for `Pull complete` / `Already exists`, so the error chunk fell through and `Successfully pulled <image>` printed unconditionally.

### Why it matters

Seen in [rstudio-pro run 33187667267](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/actions/runs/33187667267), preview leg:

```
15:58:12  Pulling image rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily...
16:00:33  Successfully pulled rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily
16:00:33  Starting Workbench container...
16:02:56  docker.errors.ImageNotFound: 404 ... No such image: rstudio/rstudio-workbench-preview:jammy-daily
```

Three separate costs:

1. The success message is a lie, and the real failure surfaces 2m23s later as `No such image` — pointing at the wrong component entirely.
2. `docker-py`'s own `images.pull()` has the same blind spot, so `containers.run()`'s automatic re-pull failed identically instead of reporting why. That re-pull is the 2m23s gap.
3. Because `pull_image()` never raised, `ensure_image()`'s fallback chain (preview registry, then local cache) was unreachable for this entire class of failure.

### Approach

Check each chunk for `error` and raise `docker.errors.APIError` with the registry's own reason, matching how `docker-py` itself handles stream errors in `models/images.py` (`if 'error' in chunk: raise ...`). `ensure_image()`'s existing `except Exception` then composes it, so the fallbacks work again and the operator sees the cause:

```
Failed to pull image: rstudio/rstudio-workbench:jammy: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit
```

### Tests

`pull_image()` and `ensure_image()` had no coverage at all. Adds four cases: a stream error raises; a clean stream still succeeds; a failed pull with no cached image surfaces the registry reason; a failed pull with a cached image falls back to it. Full suite green via `uv run test_main.py`.

### Not addressed

This makes the failure honest, it does not make it rarer — a transient registry blip will still fail the run, now with a one-line reason. A bounded retry is a separate concern and deliberately not bundled here.
